OpenGWASDB at full scale — OGS-00011

Published

November 1, 2026

The GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid Store — 3,169 Analyses, Reference-Completed · 48.1 million variants and 47.0 billion associations

ImportantWhat this measures

One Store Release over the GWAS Catalog’s European-ancestry summary statistics, built once and queried through the public API.

The release is one Store with two physical components, and every query is answered from one or both of them:

  • the Dense Component (dense/) holds a cell for each of the 14,267,257 panel variants in each of the 3,169 Analyses that come from 475 publications — 45.2 billion cells on the reference axis, observed or filled in by Reference Completion;
  • the Ragged Overflow (data.zarr/ragged/) holds, for each Analysis, the variants that Analysis observed off the panel: 33,802,661 distinct variants carrying 1,746,404,178 associations, stored against a variant index rather than a dense axis;
  • the shared variant axis (variants.tsv.gz and the ALID and rsid lookups) is what gives both components one address space.

A lookup of a panel variant reads the Dense Component. A lookup of an off-axis variant reads only the Overflow. A whole-Analysis read touches both and merges them in genomic order.

  • 166.56 GB on disk, against 1,511.69 GB of source GWAS-SSF across 3,169 files — a 9.08× reduction.
  • A top-hits query returns in 15.7 ms; a PheWAS across all 3,169 Analyses in 90.6 ms; a PheWAS of an off-axis variant in 18.2 ms.
  • Those queries need ~276 MB of resident memory. A laptop can open this Store.
  • Build and Reference Completion took 47.25 h of wall clock.

The cost is concentrated in whole-Analysis reads: returning tens of millions of associations takes tens of seconds and — on the Analysis with the largest Overflow — more than three gigabytes. Everything targeted is cheap in both time and memory.

The three component rows are the harness’s own walk of each part of the release. Between them they account for all but 17,150 bytes of the 166,556,322,972 the whole directory holds. The Shared variant axis is 2.5% of the Store, and it is what makes the two components one address space rather than two files that happen to sit together.

Measure Value
Store Release 166.56 GB across 30,085 files
Source GWAS-SSF 1,511.69 GB across 3,169 files
Reduction 9.08×
Bytes per association 3.55 B

The source is already bgzip-compressed, so this is a reduction against compressed text, not against plain text. It comes from storing z and standard error as fixed-point and residual codes rather than as text floats, from encoding the allele frequency as a residual against the reference, and from holding the variant axis once instead of repeating positions and alleles in every Analysis.

The release was built and then completed, and the records keep the two apart: build wrote the observed Store in 26.87 h on 24 workers, and complete filled the Dense Component’s imputed cells in 20.39 h on the same number of workers. Together that is 47.25 h. The remaining steps build the HM3 Indexed Variant Subset and the overview, then validate the release, and the sum of every recorded step is 66.13 h.

Each row carries the revision its step ran at, not one revision for the whole release: 70340e0 for build, indexed-subset-hm3, overview, validate, register; bc22e84 for complete, completion-indexed-subset-hm3, completion-overview, completion-validate; 44f25a9 for completion-observed-view-check, completion-register. A Store built across a change of opengwasdb is still one Store, but its parts were written by different code, and the records here are where that shows.

Hybrid against its Dense Component

A 1 Mb window × every Analysis 3.01 s 10,291,241 3.48 s 9,784,502 0.87×

10 random variants × 100 Analyses 1.73 s 119 590.8 ms 899 2.94×
100 random variants × 10 Analyses 1.73 s 239 1.27 s 765 1.36×

A Hybrid lookup does more than a panel lookup, and the gap between the two sets of columns is what it charges for the difference. It resolves every identifier the call is given — variant ALIDs and rsids, and the Analyses it is asked about — on the shared axis of 48,069,918 variants; for a lookup of named Analyses it then searches each of those Analyses’ Ragged Overflow segments in turn. A regional PheWAS across every Analysis instead reads the Overflow’s by-variant index once, then merges the two components’ rows into one genomic order. The Dense-only column is the same question asked of the reference axis’ 14,267,257 panel variants and nothing else — the price a reader pays who wants panel variants only.

The ratios are not one number called “the Overflow’s cost”. regional is faster through the Hybrid — 3.01 s against 3.48 s — on 506,739 more rows, so the twin is not the Hybrid’s time minus the Overflow’s: the two calls walk different axes and return different row sets. regional_one_analysis returns 3,000 cells either way, and its 37.5× is almost entirely identifier resolution: the Hybrid lookup resolves each of the window’s ALIDs on the shared axis one at a time before it reads any cell, and the one Overflow segment it then searches is small. The two random lookups compare different questions: their Dense draws are panel variants, which carry a cell in nearly every Analysis, so they return 899 and 765 rows against the Hybrid draws’ 119 and 239, and the ratio there compares two different questions.

The three Hybrid-only shapes

  • PheWAS of an off-axis variant — 18.2 ms for 51 rows. The variant is off the reference axis, so the Dense Component holds no row for it and the entire answer comes from the Ragged Overflow: its variant-centric index maps the variant to the 51 Analyses that observed it, without reading the other 3,118. A Dense-of-union layout would hold that variant as a row in all 3,169 columns, almost all of it padding.
  • Whole Analysis through both components — 25.86 s for 26,207,009 rows. The Hybrid facade reads the Analysis’s Dense Component column, reads its Overflow segment, and merges the two in genomic order: 11,190,536 rows from the panel and 15,016,473 from the Overflow.
  • Whole Analysis from the Dense Component alone — 21.71 s for 11,190,536 rows. This is the control that isolates the Dense path, whose EAF column carries many exception-table cells, so the difference between it and the shape above is what the Overflow costs: 4.16 s and 15,016,473 rows.

The Indexed Variant Subset is one Analysis’s statistics restricted to the HapMap3 variants — a full-result extraction for LD-score work, from a Store that holds 46,959,341,611 associations. 152 of the 1,206,903 variants in the input are absent from the Store’s axis, and 7,542 of those present hold no association for this Analysis, which is why 1,188,389 rows come back rather than 1,195,931 — at 1.72 million rows per second. The subset lives in the Hybrid root’s nested Dense Component, not beside the Overflow.

Against parsing the source file

Form Wall clock Rows Per row
pd.read_csv of 30054458-GCST006867-EFO_0001360.h.tsv.gz 6.54 s (3 repetitions) 5,030,727 1.30 µs
The Store’s whole-Analysis read of the same Analysis 20.81 s (5 repetitions) 9,869,010 2.11 µs

The file is 232,792,798 bytes and is parsed for the five columns a z/se/eaf answer needs, with beta divided by standard error into z: 6.54 s for 5,030,727 rows with a finite result. The Store answers the same Analysis genome-wide with 9,869,010 rows, 1.96× as many, because Reference Completion fills panel variants the file never reported. Per returned row the Store read is 1.62× the file parse. A whole-Analysis read is the one shape a per-file layout is built for, and the Store is competitive rather than faster here; what it adds is that the same read is one call, in the same coordinate system as every other Analysis.

Opening the Store costs 272–283 MB whichever shape follows, and that figure does not scale with the release: 3,169 Analyses and 47.0 billion associations available cost about as much resident memory as a text editor, because nothing is read until it is asked for. Query cost then follows result size, from 1.3 MB (Top hits for one Analysis (p < 5×10⁻⁸)) to 3.27 GB (One Analysis, genome-wide, both components). Targeted queries are safe to run concurrently and on modest hardware; whole-Analysis reads have to be budgeted — 30 concurrent reads at the heaviest shape’s cost would already ask for 100 GB.

The four Dense-only probes are in that table too, marked as such: the same questions asked of the reference axis alone. Their cost does not simply drop, because what they read is a panel draw and a panel draw returns a cell in nearly every Analysis — 899 rows against the Hybrid draw’s 119 for the ten-variant shape, and 257.0 MB against 56.0 MB of resident memory. The regional probe goes the same way: the component alone peaks 1.31 GB above baseline against the Hybrid call’s 1.29 GB, on 9,784,502 and 10,291,241 rows. Query cost follows result size here too, so the Dense Component is not the lighter path for every shape.

All 8 of 8 loci were found. 7 were held to p < 5×10⁻⁸ and all of them clear it. PPARG rs1801282 is the one variant the harness does not require that of — a modest-effect missense variant — and its −log10 p of 23.8 clears the bar anyway. The signs are the published ones: the TCF7L2 risk allele T carries z = +39.7, PCSK9’s R46L allele G +79.9, and APOE’s ε4-defining C +104.1.

Every one of the eight sits on the reference axis and is answered by the Dense Component, so this section checks the panel path, the allele orientation and the SE decoding. The Overflow is what the off-axis PheWAS and the whole-Analysis reads below exercise.

Pleiotropy

Two variants with well-known pleiotropic profiles, each queried across every Analysis in the Store, listing the eight strongest by |z|.

GCST002047 (educational attainment, college completion) holds odds ratios in its source beta column rather than log-odds: at this variant the source gives beta 1.001, standard error 0.011 and p 0.96, so the stored z of −91 is an artefact of reading an odds ratio as a log-odds effect. The rows below it are the list to read.

Both profiles are what the literature predicts. rs7903146 is the TCF7L2 type 2 diabetes variant, and every Analysis in its list except educational attainment is a type 2 diabetes or glycaemic trait; educational attainment is at the top of the list only through the mislabelled column described above, so that row is not evidence about this variant at all. rs429358 is the APOE ε4 allele, and its list is Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, LDL and non-HDL cholesterol, and C-reactive protein. Neither variant is special-cased in the Store: both are ordinary panel variants and each PheWAS is one call across all 3,169 Analyses.

Three positive-control IVW pairs

Exposure → Outcome Instruments from Overflow IVW β se p Cochran Q (df) Elapsed
GCST90239658 Low density lipoprotein cholesterol levels
→ GCST003116 Coronary artery disease		 451 of 97,501 0 +0.534 0.0406 1.6e-39 1,320 (450) 19.89 s
GCST90029007 Body mass index
→ GCST006867 Type 2 diabetes		 662 of 82,973 0 +0.888 0.0425 5.5e-97 2,868 (661) 18.11 s

→ GCST003116 Coronary artery disease		 654 of 109,155 0 +0.669 0.0480 3.9e-44 1,624 (653) 22.50 s

The pairs, in the words the run records for them:

  • LDL cholesterol (GLGC) -> coronary artery disease (CARDIoGRAMplusC4D): the canonical positive control
  • BMI (UK Biobank) -> type 2 diabetes (DIAGRAM/UKB): a large, well-replicated causal effect; samples overlap
  • systolic blood pressure (MVP) -> coronary artery disease: a well-replicated causal effect

Each pair starts from the exposure’s genome-wide-significant variants, prunes them to one per 1,000 kb, and reads both sides of every instrument with one lookup. All 1,767 instruments across the three pairs come from the Dense Component; the Overflow contributes 0 of them. The standard error is the random-effects one, inflated by Cochran’s Q where the instruments disagree more than their own errors allow — and they do, from 2.5× to 4.3× Q’s degrees of freedom. The whole three-pair run, including both lookups per instrument, takes 60.50 s.

An instrument is imputed when at least one of its two cells was filled by Reference Completion rather than read from a source file. Counted that way, and by which side was filled:

  • GCST90239658 → GCST003116: 28 of 451 instruments are imputed — 26 observed on the exposure and imputed on the outcome; 2 imputed on both.
  • GCST90029007 → GCST006867: 158 of 662 instruments are imputed — 139 observed on the exposure and imputed on the outcome; 19 imputed on both.
  • GCST90310294 → GCST003116: 18 of 654 instruments are imputed — 5 observed on the exposure and imputed on the outcome; 5 the other way round; 8 imputed on both.

On the side that was filled, an instrument’s β and se are the values the completion step stored, not numbers that Analysis’s source file reported. The instrument itself is still a variant on the shared axis, resolved and read the same way as any other.

The both-observed stratum reproduces the all-instrument estimate in every pair — within 10% of it — which is what the plot should show: the instruments whose two cells both come from source files carry the signal. The 5 imputed strata that have an estimate are weaker, with |β| at 0.24× to 0.63× the observed stratum’s (1 of them negative), and less certain, with standard errors 1.2× to 10.9× larger; the only one to clear p < 0.05 is Body mass index → Type 2 diabetes’s one cell observed, one imputed stratum. Their slopes are the dashed lines that do not coincide with the solid one.

This is what summary-statistic imputation predicts. An imputed z is the expected value given the observed variants around it, shrunk towards zero by the imputation’s uncertainty, so an instrument with an imputed cell understates its effect, and most imputed instruments here have an observed exposure and an imputed outcome. An MR on a Reference-Completed Store should report the both-observed estimate beside the all-instrument one.

WarningThis is not a causal estimate

The three rows above are positive controls for the query path, not findings. Their job is to show that instruments can be found, that effect signs survive the build’s allele orientation, and that standard errors propagate through a query. The estimates come out in the expected direction and magnitude, which is what a correct pipeline predicts.

They are not an epidemiological result:

  • Distance pruning is not LD clumping. Instruments are pruned by distance rather than by linkage disequilibrium, so variants in LD survive together and the weighted IVW treats them as independent. That is part of what the inflated Cochran’s Q is measuring.
  • Some pairs share samples. Where the two GWAS overlap, an instrument’s effects on exposure and outcome are correlated and the IVW variance is wrong.
  • No sensitivity analysis. There is no pleiotropy-robust estimator, no MR-Egger intercept, no Steiger filtering and no leave-one-out. A causal claim needs all of them, against properly clumped and harmonised data.

What the Store contributes here is that all three pairs read one coordinate system, in one process, in seconds.

Regional windows

Three ±500 kb windows, one per gene, each read for the single Analysis that owns the trait: every shared-axis variant in the window is looked up through the Hybrid path, so a plot holds panel cells and off-axis cells together. Grey is a cell the source reported, red one Reference Completion filled in, and a triangle one only the Ragged Overflow holds.

  • TCF7L2 (GCST006867, Type 2 diabetes) — 1,363 observed and 1,635 imputed cells, with no Overflow cells in the window; 91 imputed and 137 observed cells clear p < 5×10⁻⁸, every imputed one has an observed one within 12.5 kb, and the strongest imputed cell (247.2) is 24.2 kb from the lead (344.4), so the filled cells trace the observed association rather than adding a peak of their own.
  • FTO (GCST90029007, Body mass index) — 3,148 observed and 402 imputed cells, plus 42 Overflow cells (triangles) the Analysis observed off the panel; 27 imputed and 323 observed cells clear p < 5×10⁻⁸, every imputed one has an observed one within 2.7 kb, and the strongest imputed cell (309.7) is 5.4 kb from the lead (324.1), so the filled cells trace the observed association rather than adding a peak of their own.
  • PCSK9 (GCST90239658, Low density lipoprotein cholesterol levels) — 4,597 observed and 152 imputed cells, plus 205 Overflow cells (triangles) the Analysis observed off the panel; 20 imputed and 1,107 observed cells clear p < 5×10⁻⁸, every imputed one has an observed one within 2.7 kb, and the strongest imputed cell (188.7) is 13.8 kb from the lead (1,389.3), so the filled cells trace the observed association rather than adding a peak of their own.

That is what to look for in each plot: the red points should sit on the same peaks as the blue ones, at the shoulder heights the completed values predict, and not form isolated towers away from an observed signal. Where triangles appear, they should fall inside the same association, since the Overflow holds what that Analysis observed off the panel rather than a different signal.

Limitations

  • Warm page cache. Each shape is timed after one warm-up call, so the medians describe a warm operating-system cache. A first, cold query against a region or an Analysis is bounded by disk instead, and that cost is not measured here.
  • A shared host whose load was not controlled. The artifact records no host load, so these medians cannot be read as quiet-machine numbers. What it does record is the spread: every p95 is within 16% of its median, so the run was steady while it ran, but nothing here says what else the machine was doing.
  • One Store, at one revision. One Hybrid Store Release, on one host and one filesystem, measured with one opengwasdb tree (e8938731ac79). Nothing here compares the Hybrid layout against a Dense-of-union build of the same data, and nothing repeats the run on another machine.
  • The Store carries a Release Erratum for eight associations (opengwas/opengwasdb-stores#401; the builder’s narrowing is opengwas/opengwasdb#338). Their source standard error exceeds the range of a float16 plane, so it is stored as +inf beside a finite z, and β = z × se reads as infinity although the source value was finite. Validation reports this as a warning rather than a failure, and the query path’s lookup keeps only cells where z and se are both finite, so those eight associations do not come back from a lookup. Read them from the se plane, or from the erratum, not from a lookup.
  • Two Analyses carry mislabelled effect columns. GCST002047 (educational attainment, college completion) stores odds ratios where beta belongs, and GCST004461 (low-grade serous ovarian cancer) stores log-odds in its odds_ratio column, so taking its log a second time inflates z — its source p of 0.32 at rs569167217 is stored as z 12.4. Both are being raised with the owner, and their stored statistics should not be used until they are rebuilt.
  • Memory sampling resolution. The peak sampler polls every 5 ms, so an allocation spike shorter than that inside a sub-millisecond query can be missed. That affects the shapes whose cost is about a megabyte anyway; the multi-gigabyte flights last far longer than the polling interval.

pixi run -e dev python benchmarks/benchmark_ogs00011_hybrid.py

    --manifest /data/opengwasdb/stores/OGS-00011/work/analyses.tsv

The commit names the checkout’s HEAD when the run finished; the fingerprint is a sha256 over the package’s Python sources, so it names the code itself and would differ if the tree had been edited after the commit. Every figure on this page was read from the artifact at render time — the page holds no copy of the measurement.
